title: Requirements Engineering with Quarto-Needs
text:
1 Engineering Quarto-Needs with Quarto-Needs
This book is a self-hosted engineering case study: Quarto-Needs is used to specify, explain, govern, verify, and explore the engineering of Quarto-Needs itself.
The case study demonstrates how requirements engineering concepts connect inside the product that implements them.
The canonical engineering graph is authored in English. Every chapter has a Brazilian Portuguese sibling (*.pt-BR.qmd) that translates titles and narrative while preserving the same IDs, types, statuses, attributes, and relations. The pre-render step rejects semantic drift between languages.

title: Requirements Engineering with Quarto-Needs
text:
1.1 What to look for
The book is read from stakeholder concern toward realization and evidence:
Stakeholder need
      ↓ motivates
System requirement
      ↓ is refined into
Functional / non-functional requirement
      ↓ is addressed by
Architecture decision
      ↓ scopes
Component or interface
      ↓ is realized in
Source module
      ↓ is verified through
Test case
      ↓ produces / supports
Evidence
That reading order is deliberately not the same thing as the direction of every stored relation. For example, the canonical derivation relation is authored as:
Functional requirement --derives-from--> System requirement
System requirement     --derives-from--> Stakeholder need
Quarto-Needs can still traverse the derivation chain pedagogically from the stakeholder need toward the derived requirements because traversal direction is semantic metadata published by the core rather than guessed from raw edge orientation.
This is not a synthetic taxonomy. The objects describe capabilities and architectural choices that exist in the repository today.

title: Requirements Engineering with Quarto-Needs
text:
1.2 The learning path

System Context establishes the system boundary, actors, and external tools.
Drivers introduces stakeholder needs and system requirements.
Requirements refines those drivers into functional and quality requirements.
Architecture records the components, interfaces, risks, and ADRs that shape the implementation.
Implementation traces approved obligations into real Python and JavaScript source modules.
Verification connects requirements and decisions to executable checks and evidence.
Interoperability federates OSLC and GitHub external state as read-only, provenance-bound projections without importing remote semantics into the canonical graph.
Traceability uses the interactive graph as an analysis instrument rather than a static diagram.
Change teaches baseline, structured diff, and semantic impact analysis.

The stakeholder needs that motivate everything else:

STK-001 — Engineering teams need lifecycle-wide traceability approved
STK-002 — Engineers need the engineering model to remain readable documentation approved
STK-003 — Teams need reproducible governance in Git and CI approved
STK-004 — Architecture choices need durable rationale and traceability approved
STK-005 — Multilingual teams need one engineering graph approved
STK-006 — Engineering teams need standards-based federation without semantic drift approved
STK-007 — Engineering teams need requirements linked to live issue-tracker state without importing the tracker approved
STK-008 — Quarto authors need the extension to be the whole installation approved

The graph is progressively enhanced: the static representation remains available, while the HTML view adds semantic traversal, filtering, root paths, edge inspection, collapse/expand, and fixed spacing.

title: 2  System context: where requirements come from
text:
2.1 System boundary
A requirements model becomes easier to understand when the reader first knows the system boundary, its actors, and the external surfaces through which engineering work enters and leaves the product.
Quarto-Needs is not the documentation itself and it is not the browser graph. It is the semantic engine between authored engineering sources and the views, checks, and automation that consume them.

crumbs: 2  System context: where requirements come from

title: 2  System context: where requirements come from
text:
2.2 Primary actors
Requirements engineers author needs, requirements, relations, rationale, and governance policy. Architects record architecture decisions and scope. Developers implement the obligations and keep source modules traceable. Reviewers inspect coverage, decisions, impact, and evidence. CI automation executes the same deterministic analysis without becoming a separate semantic authority.
The external tools also have deliberately narrow roles. Git versions text and generated evidence; Quarto renders documents; BabelQuarto projects localized presentation; the browser explores an already resolved graph.
crumbs: 2  System context: where requirements come from

title: 2  System context: where requirements come from
section: 2.3 Why this matters for the model
text:
2.3 Why this matters for the model
The stakeholder needs in the next chapter are therefore not abstract personas. They arise from concrete tensions at this boundary: humans need readable documents while automation needs formal semantics; multilingual readers need translated presentation while the engineering graph must remain singular; interactive exploration needs rich metadata while public projections must remain bounded and safe.
The first derivation layer can be explored directly below. The view starts at the stakeholder need and follows the catalog’s semantic traversal direction toward requirements; the stored derives-from relation itself points in the opposite direction, from the derived requirement to its source need.

Quarto-Needs shall provision and invoke an exact, compatible semantic engine from the activated extension during ordinary rendering, without a global package installation, a CLI on PATH, or a user-authored pre-render.

The system requirements establish broad obligations. This chapter refines them into capabilities that can be implemented and quality constraints that shape how those capabilities must behave.

text:

functional-requirement approved critical


Quarto-Needs shall parse .need declarations from QMD sources into structured engineering object declarations with stable identity and source locations.

parser authoring graph

Text-first authoring is only useful if the semantic core can recover structured objects deterministically from ordinary documentation sources.

section: FUN-009 · Collapse the page margin TOC without obscuring navigation
text:
FUN-009 · Collapse the page margin TOC without obscuring navigation

functional-requirement approved medium


The HTML extension shall provide an optional persistent control that collapses and restores the page margin table of contents, reclaims content width while collapsed, and positions the expanded-state control entirely outside the TOC so it does not obscure the title or navigation items.

quarto toc sidebar usability progressive-enhancement


Rationale
A collapsible margin TOC is only useful if the control itself does not interfere with the navigation surface it manages. Its positioning is therefore treated as engineering behavior with an executable regression contract, not as incidental decorative styling.

section: ADR-001 · Keep Python as the semantic authority
text:
ADR-001 · Keep Python as the semantic authority

architecture-decision accepted 2026-08-29



Context and Problem Statement
The product has a Python analysis core, Lua rendering filters, and JavaScript interaction. If each layer defines engineering meaning independently, equivalent views can drift.

python semantics architecture



Decision Drivers

one source of engineering semantics;
deterministic analysis;
testability outside the browser;
presentation layers that remain replaceable.



Considered Options

duplicate relation maps in every client;
resolve semantics in Lua during rendering;
resolve semantics once in Python and publish semantic projections.



Decision Outcome
Python owns engineering semantics. Lua and JavaScript consume relation metadata and other semantic projections emitted by the core.


Consequences
Public projection contracts become more important, but presentation clients become simpler and cannot silently redefine engineering meaning.


Confirmation
TC-001 confirms the canonical snapshot and TC-008 confirms relation-catalog semantics.


Need relations



Addresses

NFR-005 — Resolve engineering semantics in the core only


RISK-001 — Semantic meaning diverges across core and presentation layers

SYS-003 — Provide deterministic validation and quality gates

Applies to

Generate one bounded public projection and derive static diagram/table output and interactive exploration from that same artifact.


Consequences
The public graph schema becomes a stable contract and interactive features must operate as progressive enhancement over it.

TC-006 validates the public projection contract and TC-010 checks the exploration assets.

section: ADR-007 · Treat the margin TOC control as persistent progressive enhancement
text:
ADR-007 · Treat the margin TOC control as persistent progressive enhancement

architecture-decision accepted 2026-08-30



Context and Problem Statement
The page margin TOC can consume useful reading width, but a collapse control positioned over the TOC undermines the navigation it is intended to improve.

quarto toc sidebar usability progressive-enhancement



Decision Drivers

preserve native Quarto navigation semantics;
make the feature optional and browser-only;
persist the reader’s collapsed state;
reclaim content width while collapsed;
never obscure the expanded TOC with the control itself.



Decision Outcome
Implement the control as JavaScript progressive enhancement. Persist state in local storage, use Quarto’s fullcontent class only while the extension forces the collapsed state, and position the expanded control completely outside the margin sidebar with an explicit gap.


Consequences
The static document remains usable without JavaScript, while HTML readers gain a persistent space-reclaiming control. Positioning becomes an explicit regression contract rather than incidental CSS/DOM behavior.


Confirmation
TC-014 checks persistence/full-content behavior and verifies that the expanded control is positioned by button.offsetWidth + gap, never by the old half-width overlap.


Need relations



Addresses

Applies to

Confirmed by

text:
ADR-011 · Document Quarto-Needs itself through explicit viewpoints, indexed arc42-lite

architecture-decision accepted 2026-09-02



Context and Problem Statement
ARCHITECTURE.md and this self-hosted example both describe the system, but neither page declares its audience, the concern it answers, or when it must be revisited. As the product grew from a single pipeline into CLI/core/Quarto/LSP/VS Code/interoperability surfaces, an undeclared set of ad hoc pages risks duplicating content and drifting silently.

documentation architecture viewpoints arc42



Decision Drivers

give every architecture page an explicit audience, concern, and update trigger;
avoid forcing one notation (C4, UML, or 4+1) to answer every question;
keep the index navigable without becoming a second copy of this case study.



Decision Outcome
Organize notes/architecture/ as a small set of ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010-style viewpoints, indexed by an arc42-lite structure. Each page records its audience, concern, notation, and source in viewpoints.md; diagrams are chosen per concern rather than committing the whole set to one modeling language.


Consequences
The documentation set gains a stable table of contents and a contract per page, at the cost of keeping viewpoints.md current whenever a page’s purpose changes.


Confirmation
TC-002 confirms the presentation/rendering path this documentation set builds on.


Need relations



Addresses

STK-002 — Engineers need the engineering model to remain readable documentation

section: ADR-012 · Model architectural roles as configurable types, not a fixed enumeration
text:
ADR-012 · Model architectural roles as configurable types, not a fixed enumeration

architecture-decision accepted 2026-09-02



Context and Problem Statement
Phase 6 needed system/container/component/actor/external-system roles for C4 views. A fixed Python enum for architectural roles would hardcode one project’s vocabulary into the core, contradicting the existing decision to keep traceability as a typed property graph with project-declared types (ADR-003).

architecture types extensibility



Decision Outcome
Architectural roles are ordinary entries under [types.*] in project configuration, validated the same way as every other type, never a hardcoded enumeration in config.py. ARC001 and the C4 projection match on these configured types plus the fixed C4 layer order, never on a Python-level role constant.


Consequences
A project can rename or extend its architectural vocabulary without a core code change; C4 support depends on a project actually declaring the expected types, which the C4 projection and ARC001 already report explicitly when a focus type is unsupported.


Confirmation
TC-004 confirms decision and rule governance, including ARC001’s layer-adjacency checks.


Need relations

text:
ADR-013 · Represent architecture hierarchy and containment through a first-class part-of relation

architecture-decision accepted 2026-09-02



Context and Problem Statement
decomposes already expressed parent-to-child containment, but nothing let a child self-declare its parent: every container had to enumerate its own components by hand, an error-prone, one-directional bookkeeping burden.

architecture hierarchy relations



Decision Outcome
Add part-of as decomposes’s genuine inverse (child-authored, (part, whole) roles, its own v1_name so relation_policies can target one direction independently). Enforce fixed-layer adjacency (system > container > component > source-module) with the ARC001 rule over both authored directions.


Consequences
Components and source modules author their own placement; ARC001 catches layer-skipping or same-layer edges as a structural error, and non-C4 types are simply ignored by the rule rather than rejected.


Confirmation
TC-004.

section: ADR-014 · Reuse part-of instead of introducing a separate realized-by/realizes relation
text:
ADR-014 · Reuse part-of instead of introducing a separate realized-by/realizes relation

architecture-decision accepted 2026-09-02



Context and Problem Statement
An external documentation-strategy review proposed adding an ArchitectureElement realized-by ImplementationArtifact relation (and its inverse realizes) to connect components to the source modules that implement them, reasoning that containment and “is realized by” are conceptually distinct. By the time this decision was recorded, part-of already connected every source-module to its owning component (see implementation.qmd), and ARC001 already treats that edge as the bottom rung of the same fixed C4 layer ladder used for container/system.

architecture relations traceability



Considered Options

introduce realized-by/realizes as a new relation family, kept parallel to part-of;
keep part-of as the single relation connecting a source module to its owning component, exactly as it already connects a component to its container and a container to its system.



Decision Outcome
Do not introduce realized-by/realizes. part-of already means “the child sits inside this parent at the next C4 layer up” for every layer, including source-module -> component. A second relation expressing the same fact between the same two objects would let the two edges disagree with no rule capable of detecting the contradiction, and would fragment ARC001’s single layer-adjacency check across two relation families.


Consequences
Architecture-to-implementation traceability continues to read entirely through part-of plus implements/implemented-by (code to requirement); no new relation, rule, or projection code exists for this concern.


Confirmation
TC-004.


Need relations



Addresses

RISK-001 — Semantic meaning diverges across core and presentation layers

Applies to

COMP-ANALYSIS — Semantic analysis core


COMP-RULES — Governance rule engine

Confirmed by

TC-004 — Architecture-decision governance regression

text:
ADR-015 · Derive C4/architecture projections from the canonical snapshot, never hand-author them

architecture-decision accepted 2026-09-02



Context and Problem Statement
A hand-maintained C4 diagram drifts the moment the underlying part-of/depends-on graph changes, and a second, independently authored diagram risks disagreeing with the engineering graph it claims to depict.

architecture c4 projection



Decision Outcome
build_c4_view computes every C4 level as one select_graph depth-1 call over an allowlisted set of relations for that level; c4_mermaid_source/c4_code_table_markdown render that projection as text; write_c4_projections writes one JSON file per view under .quarto-needs/graphs/. No C4 view is authored directly; the need-c4 shortcode only ever reads a pre-rendered projection file.


Consequences
Every C4 diagram in this documentation set is reproducible from the graph and cannot silently diverge from it; adding an object or part-of edge is sufficient to update the corresponding view on the next build.


Confirmation
TC-006.

section: ADR-017 · Draw an explicit boundary between authored architecture declarations and generated projections
text:
ADR-017 · Draw an explicit boundary between authored architecture declarations and generated projections

architecture-decision accepted 2026-09-02



Context and Problem Statement
Generated files (.quarto-needs/needs.json, .quarto-needs/graphs/*.json, generated-index.lua) live inside the same project tree as authored .qmd declarations. Without an explicit rule, a contributor could hand-edit a generated file, or a generated file could be mistaken for a second authoring surface.

architecture generated-artifacts boundary



Decision Outcome
Every path under a project’s .quarto-needs/ output directory is generated-only: the CLI build step recreates it in full on every run, generated-index.lua is explicitly excluded from the extension-asset sync so it is never treated as an authoring source, and stale c4-*.json files are removed before a projection is rewritten. notes/architecture/generated/ follows the same rule for this documentation set’s own diagrams.


Consequences
Reviewers and contributors can rely on “is it under .quarto-needs/ (or notes/architecture/generated/)?” as a sufficient test for “may I hand-edit this file?”; the answer is always no.


Confirmation
TC-006.


Need relations



Addresses

SYS-006 — Publish bounded semantic graph projections for exploration

section: ADR-018 · Classify execution units (system, container) separately from logical components
text:
ADR-018 · Classify execution units (system, container) separately from logical components

architecture-decision accepted 2026-09-02



Context and Problem Statement
This example’s own component objects mix logical responsibility (parser, rule engine) with what are really deployable/executable units; a naive C4 projection that mapped every type=component to a C4 Component would blur the distinction between “runs as a process” and “is a logical piece of a process.”

architecture c4 execution-units



Decision Outcome
system and container are configured as distinct types representing deployable/executable units; component remains the logical decomposition inside a container. build_c4_view requires a system focus for Context/Container and a container focus for Component, so a logical component can never itself be treated as a container boundary.


Consequences
Adding a new deployable unit means declaring a new container (or system), not repurposing an existing component; ARC001’s fixed layer order (system > container > component > source-module) enforces this separation structurally.


Confirmation
TC-004.

section: ADR-019 · Provision a project-local managed runtime through an extension bootstrap
text:
ADR-019 · Provision a project-local managed runtime through an extension bootstrap

architecture-decision accepted 2026-09-03



Context and Problem Statement
The extension needs a Python semantic engine, but users install only the extension. The old contract asked for three separate pieces — a global pip install, a CLI on PATH, and a hand-authored pre-render — each one an independent chance to be missing, stale, or wrong for the extension’s version.

distribution extension bootstrap managed-runtime



Decision Outcome
The extension manifest contributes the project pre-render itself. A standard-library bootstrap provisions quarto-needs==<extension version> into .quarto-needs/runtime/<version>/<interpreter-identity>/ through staged, lock-protected, atomic installs, validates the actually imported version, and invokes the same canonical pre-render service the CLI uses. A valid cached runtime renders offline; a provisioning failure fails the render with the needed version, the missing runtime, and both recovery actions.


Consequences
Rendering has exactly one installation responsibility, and extension and engine versions cannot drift silently. First-use provisioning still requires Python and pip, which remain documented platform prerequisites; the residual availability risk is carried explicitly by RISK-013 rather than hidden.


Confirmation
TC-025 proves the clean first render, TC-026 the offline second render, and TC-029 concurrent-safe provisioning.


Need relations



Addresses

RISK-013 — First-use provisioning depends on Python, pip, and package availability


SYS-009 — Deliver the semantic engine through the activated extension itself

Applies to

COMP-EXTENSION — Quarto presentation extension

Confirmed by

TC-025 — Extension-first clean render


TC-026 — Offline second render


TC-029 — Concurrent provisioning

section: ADR-020 · Publish a narrow first supported release
text:
ADR-020 · Publish a narrow first supported release

architecture-decision accepted 2026-09-09



Context and Problem Statement
A single maintainer cannot promise the same release stability for the core engineering workflow and every external integration. The existing v0.1.0 tag reached TestPyPI but failed its installation rehearsal; the current candidate is 0.1.1.

distribution release support



Decision Outcome
Release 0.1.1 supports the documented core analysis, change reports, evidence, LSP, exports and Quarto views. OSLC, GitHub Issues, migration adapters, the VS Code client and C4 projections remain experimental. Preserve v0.1.0; publish a new immutable version only after clean distribution checks and a TestPyPI rehearsal. Detailed stability tiers are a subsequent policy change.


Consequences
Release validation covers the supported surface; experimental functionality does not expand that promise. Package schemas and canonical extension assets accompany both distributions, while the extension remains independently installable through Quarto.


Confirmation
TC-025, TC-032.

title: 7  Verification: proving the engineering claims
text:
7.1 Test cases
Traceability is incomplete if requirements terminate at design. This chapter models verification as first-class engineering objects and connects successful tests to explicit evidence.
The test cases below correspond to real classes of regression checks in the repository. Twenty-three executable bindings now cover architecture-decision governance, multilingual semantic parity, public graph safety, named graph views, change impact, margin-TOC usability, the OSLC federation path (orchestration, reconciliation identity, bounded query, member observation, import plan), the GitHub issues adapter (identity, cache, pagination, reconciliation, rate limits), and extension-first distribution (clean render, offline reuse, version-skew isolation, corruption, concurrency, spaces in paths, Quarto floor). make evidence-self-example executes those tests, writes deterministic provider output, attests it against the current engineering snapshot, and validates .quarto-needs/evidence/pytest.json before the self-hosted book is rendered.

SYS-007 · Federate OSLC requirements through a bounded read-only adapter

system-requirement approved high


Quarto-Needs shall discover OSLC Requirements Management services, execute explicitly selected read-only Query Capabilities, materialize selected query members as independently provenance-bearing observations, and reconcile observed external resources through a bounded federation layer that preserves external identity, cache provenance, and trust without importing remote semantics into the canonical graph automatically.

interoperability oslc federation provenance


Rationale
Federation is useful only if remote state remains distinguishable from authored project truth and failures remain explainable.

text:
FUN-011 · Reconcile external requirements only through explicit identity bindings

functional-requirement approved high


Quarto-Needs shall compare observed external requirements with canonical objects without mutating either side and shall treat an explicit external-resource-URI to canonical-ID binding as the only identity bridge. Matching titles or external identifiers shall never create an implicit merge.

oslc reconciliation identity conflict


Rationale
Provider identifiers and display fields can be reused, mutable, or locally ambiguous. Reconciliation must surface unbound resources, stale or rejected observations, missing local targets, duplicate bindings, and field differences before any future import operation is allowed.

FUN-012 · Execute an explicitly selected OSLC Query Capability without crawling members

functional-requirement approved high


Quarto-Needs shall execute a bounded HTTP GET against an explicitly selected OSLC Query Capability, parse the query-result container deterministically, enforce a maximum member count, preserve query-response provenance, and report member URIs without recursively dereferencing them.

oslc query query-capability read-only bounded


Rationale
Discovery is not sufficient for practical federation, but query execution must not silently turn into unbounded Linked Data crawling. Query results therefore remain a resource-discovery projection; authoritative member observation is a separate bounded operation.

FUN-013 · Materialize selected OSLC query members as independently provenance-bearing observations

functional-requirement approved high


Quarto-Needs shall fetch query-member URIs individually through the existing bounded transport/cache policy, normalize each fetched representation, enforce explicit fan-out and per-resource node limits, and create external requirement observations whose digest, retrieval time, trust state, validators, and resource identity derive from the bytes actually observed for that member.

oslc observation provenance member-fetch bounded


Rationale
A query container may include inline member data, but its response digest is not the digest of every member resource. Independent retrieval preserves the provenance boundary required for trustworthy reconciliation and any future reviewed import plan.

non-functional-requirement approved critical


OSLC federation shall enforce byte/time/redirect/node/member budgets, reject cross-origin redirects, prevent implicit remote JSON-LD context loading and recursive member crawling, preserve content digests and historical observations, distinguish query-response provenance from member-resource provenance, and never hide authentication failures or identity conflicts behind stale cache fallback or heuristic matching.

oslc security provenance offline determinism


Rationale
External integration expands the trust boundary and therefore requires stronger failure, provenance, identity, and traversal contracts than local projection alone.

text:
ADR-008 · Keep the first OSLC federation path read-only, bounded, and cache-provenanced

architecture-decision accepted 2026-08-30



Context and Problem Statement
OSLC introduces external identity, authentication, mutable remote representations, linked-data serialization, caching, query capabilities, and provider-specific failure modes. Treating those concerns as ordinary local objects or automatically traversing every discovered link would blur the trust boundary.

oslc federation read-only security



Decision Drivers

preserve the canonical Quarto-Needs graph as semantic authority;
make external identity and observed bytes independently auditable;
prevent hidden network activity during RDF normalization;
prevent credentials from crossing redirect origins or entering persistent artifacts;
support deterministic offline behavior without silently accepting stale state;
prevent discovery/query execution from becoming recursive Linked Data crawling;
distinguish query-container evidence from independently fetched member-resource evidence.



Decision Outcome
Implement OSLC as a read-only adapter. HTTP uses GET only with explicit budgets and same-origin redirects. Cached bytes are content-addressed by SHA-256 and historical observations are retained. RDF normalization performs no implicit remote context fetches. Query execution requires an explicitly selected query base, limits member count, and reports member URIs without recursively fetching them. A separate bounded observation step may fetch selected members individually and records provenance from each member’s actual representation bytes. Discovery, query results, member observations, Resource Shapes, and reconciliation inputs remain external projections and are not merged into the canonical graph.


Consequences
The adapter can discover, query, observe, and analyze reconciliation safely before synchronization exists. Canonical import and all remote writes remain deliberately deferred.


Confirmation
TC-015 exercises the complete network-free discovery orchestration path; TC-017 exercises bounded query execution and response provenance; TC-018 exercises independent member observation and per-resource provenance; TC-019 exercises the reviewed, non-mutating import-plan directives derived from that observation and reconciliation.

text:
ADR-009 · Require explicit URI-to-canonical-ID bindings for OSLC reconciliation

architecture-decision accepted 2026-08-30



Context and Problem Statement
A remote OSLC requirement can expose an identifier or title that happens to match a local object even when the two resources are unrelated. Automatically treating such similarity as identity would permit silent aliasing across independent authorities.

oslc reconciliation identity conflict



Decision Drivers

preserve external resource URI as the primary remote identity;
make every bridge into canonical identity explicit and reviewable;
reject stale or rejected observations before reconciliation;
expose duplicate bindings and missing local targets as conflicts;
keep comparison separate from mutation.



Decision Outcome
Reconciliation is a pure analysis step. Only an explicit mapping from external resource URI to canonical Quarto-Needs ID can yield a matched item. External identifiers and titles are comparison data only. Unbound resources remain unbound, and field differences are reported without changing the snapshot.


Consequences
This is intentionally more conservative than heuristic import. A future import command may consume an accepted reconciliation plan, but it cannot infer identity by itself and it cannot bypass provenance/trust checks.


Confirmation
TC-016 proves that a matching external identifier alone remains unbound and therefore cannot create an implicit canonical identity.

text:
ADR-010 · Keep the GitHub issues path read-only, bounded, and discovery-separated

architecture-decision accepted 2026-08-31



Context and Problem Statement
GitHub’s issues API returns pull requests alongside issues, rewrites pagination URLs from /repos/{owner}/{repo} to /repositories/{id} with cursor parameters, includes full inline issue data in list responses, and rate-limits clients with 403/429 responses. Treating any of those as canonical requirements data, following pagination without budgets, or flattening rate limits into generic errors would blur the trust boundary.

github federation read-only security



Decision Drivers

reuse OSLC’s source-agnostic identity, observation, reconciliation, and import-plan contracts instead of forking them;
keep discovered numbers separate from independently fetched, provenance-bound observations;
validate server-provided pagination targets by origin, never by path, because GitHub legitimately rewrites its own Link targets;
make truncation, malformed pagination, pull-request conflation, and rate-limit exhaustion explicit rather than guessed;
keep the transport free of retry policy: report the server’s retry facts and let the caller decide.



Decision Outcome
GitHub federation is a read-only adapter composed of a bounded JSON transport with rate-limit classification, an opt-in content-addressed cache with conditional requests, issue/projection normalization that rejects pull requests, discovery and bounded multi-page traversal that stay numbers-only, and reconciliation/import planning through the unchanged OSLC contracts. List data is never promoted into observations; pagination targets are origin-checked; rate limits raise a distinguished, retry-informing error.


Consequences
The adapter can discover, traverse, observe, reconcile, and plan imports safely before any synchronization exists. Canonical import and all remote writes remain deliberately deferred, and a rate-limit retry policy is caller-owned until a command needs one.


Confirmation
TC-020 exercises fetch-compose-normalize with exact-byte provenance; TC-021 exercises the conditional-request 304 reuse path; TC-022 exercises bounded traversal across GitHub’s rewritten pagination targets with honest truncation; TC-024 exercises rate-limit exhaustion classification against real header shapes.

9.2 1. Where did a requirement come from?
Select a requirement such as FUN-004, choose the derivation traversal profile, and inspect its parents. The path explains how interactive graph exploration traces back through SYS-002 / SYS-006 to stakeholder needs.

9.7 6. Why is this node visible?
Use Path to root after focusing a node. The browser follows the traversal direction published by the Python relation catalog. It does not guess parent/child meaning from Cytoscape edge orientation.
Click an edge to inspect:

canonical relation;
semantic family;
semantic traversal direction;
source and target roles;
impact direction;
active traversal context;
safe relative declaration provenance.

The inspector is therefore an explanation of the graph, not merely a tooltip.

title: 9  Traceability: investigate the product as an engineering graph
section: 9.8 7. Use traversal profiles as engineering lenses
text:
9.8 7. Use traversal profiles as engineering lenses
Traversal profiles are not cosmetic presets. They expose different questions over the same canonical graph:

derivation — where did this obligation come from?
decision — which engineering drivers, scope, lineage, and confirmation explain this choice?
architecture — which architecture elements and implementation relations participate?
verification — which tests and evidence support the claim?
risk — which constraints and mitigations shape the engineering response?
traceability — show the broad semantic chain.

Try combining a profile with Type, Status, and Family filters rather than treating every graph as one all-purpose picture.

9.9 8. What happens if this object changes?
The same typed relations used for documentation support baseline comparison and impact propagation. The next chapter uses FUN-005, the three comparison modules, TC-011, and EVD-011 to turn a version change into an auditable engineering-impact question.
That is the deeper purpose of requirements-as-code: version history is interpreted through engineering semantics rather than treated only as textual diff.

title: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact
text:
10.1 The historical product change
Requirements engineering does not end when the first coherent graph is approved. The difficult question is what a change means for the rest of the system. Quarto-Needs therefore treats comparison as an engineering workflow rather than a textual Git diff.
This chapter uses a real Quarto-Needs change rather than a hypothetical one: the margin table-of-contents control that was corrected after its expanded-state button overlapped the page TOC.
The original UI correction is commit ba4655d72d3b0e9fc926a2d31c77c7705efd00b2 (fix: improve graph dark theme and TOC toggle), whose parent is 77eaaf91d0127fffe974b449e5ee9718861da552.
That commit changed _extensions/quarto-needs/margin-sidebar.js: the expanded-state button had been positioned by subtracting only half of its width from the TOC boundary. The fix introduced an explicit 8 px gap and subtracts the complete button width, keeping the control entirely outside the TOC.
That is the code-history trigger for this case. At the time of that historical commit, however, the newer self-hosted engineering model did not yet contain the complete FUN-009 → ADR-007 → SRC-MARGIN-SIDEBAR → TC-014 → EVD-014 chain. A professional tutorial should not pretend otherwise.

title: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact
text:
10.3 A reproducible semantic Git range
To demonstrate Git-native engineering analysis with valid models on both sides, this repository contains a later canonical clarification of FUN-009:
base  ba69e62cf9ba4a0fb186a28e6e87649c1462f2dd
head  53dc04bf6bdd98a2f8143964684d20464d6264f6
The head clarifies in the requirement rationale that positioning is engineering behavior protected by an executable regression contract, not incidental decorative styling. All object identities and traceability links already exist in both states, so this range can be materialized and analyzed deterministically.
Set it once in a shell:
RANGE=ba69e62cf9ba4a0fb186a28e6e87649c1462f2dd..53dc04bf6bdd98a2f8143964684d20464d6264f6
crumbs: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact

title: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact
text:
10.4 Step 1 — inspect the engineering diff
quarto-needs --root examples/quarto-needs \
  diff --git "$RANGE"
For machine consumers:
quarto-needs --root examples/quarto-needs \
  diff --git "$RANGE" --format json
Unlike a text patch, the result identifies the changed engineering object (FUN-009) and the authored fields that changed. Both refs are extracted with git archive and analyzed independently; the working tree is not checked out or mutated.
Quarto-Needs uses the head commit timestamp as the common reference epoch for both materialized states. This prevents the same Git range from producing different date-sensitive results merely because it is analyzed on another day.
crumbs: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact

title: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact
text:
10.5 Step 2 — inspect explicit impact paths
quarto-needs --root examples/quarto-needs \
  impact --git "$RANGE"
Impact traverses the union of the two engineering graphs, following the catalog’s canonical impact directions. The result is a set of explicit paths, not a synthetic risk score.
For this case, downstream review attention includes the verification/evidence side of the chain. The exact result is computed from the graph rather than hard-coded as a policy rule.
crumbs: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact

title: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact
text:
10.6 Step 3 — derive suspect traceability
quarto-needs --root examples/quarto-needs \
  suspect --git "$RANGE" --format json
A suspect claim is derived state, not a persisted suspect=true flag. Each claim carries a witness:
origin + change
    ↓
explicit relation path
    ↓
affected object + semantic role
A reviewer therefore sees not only that a test or evidence object needs renewed attention, but why it became suspect and through which relations.

title: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact
section: 10.8 Step 5 — project the same analysis into GitHub CI
text:
10.8 Step 5 — project the same analysis into GitHub CI
The GitHub projection does not call GitHub APIs and does not own engineering semantics. It converts the canonical PR report into CI-friendly surfaces.
Step-summary Markdown:
quarto-needs --root examples/quarto-needs \
  github-report --git "$RANGE" --format markdown
Workflow annotations:
quarto-needs --root examples/quarto-needs \
  github-report --git "$RANGE" --format annotations
Structured check projection:
quarto-needs --root examples/quarto-needs \
  github-report --git "$RANGE" --format json
The repository CI uses the same surfaces on pull requests: full Git history is fetched, base/head SHAs are supplied by the PR event, the engineering summary is appended to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, and escaped annotations are emitted into the workflow log.

title: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact
section: 10.9 Why two historical references are useful
text:
10.9 Why two historical references are useful
This example deliberately preserves two truthful histories:

Product implementation history — 77eaaf91…ba4655d7, where the JavaScript overlap bug was actually fixed.
Executable engineering-model history — ba69e62c…53dc04bf, where a complete, valid self-hosted graph can be compared on both sides and the change can be propagated through requirements, decisions, implementation, tests, and evidence.

Conflating those histories would make the documentation look simpler but less accurate. Quarto-Needs instead keeps provenance explicit.
crumbs: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact

title: 10  Change: from version history to engineering impact
text:
10.10 Review questions
A useful change review should be able to answer:

Which stakeholder/system concern still motivates the changed requirement?
Which ADRs are candidates for reconsideration?
Which logical components and source modules implement the affected obligation?
Which verification cases need to be rerun or changed?
Which evidence is now suspect, stale, or must be regenerated?
Which quality gates or findings changed?
What exact graph path justifies every downstream review claim?

This is the point at which requirements-as-code becomes more than storing requirements in Git: the versioned graph itself participates in engineering reasoning.
